title: One Tree — the input architecture
summary: Collapse the app's 16 hand-written per-surface pointer-dispatch functions into one tree walk; fixes the toast pointer bug and makes any layer (incl. plugin overlays) receive input.
description:
The app delivers pointer input through 16 hand-written per-surface dispatch functions (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs: 8 chrome + 4 pane-header + 3 pane-viewport; plus dispatch_modal_pointer) and has NO input pass for ordinary layers at all — heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs runs rebuild/layout/paint and never input.

This phase collapses that into ONE retained tree with one dispatch/layout/paint/hint walk, using the capture→target→bubble traversal heca-grid-ui already provides (`dispatch()` in heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs). Overlays, modals and pane headers become nodes; adding a surface becomes adding a child. Done properly this DELETES the 16 functions rather than adding a 17th.

═══ ⚠️ A WIDGET NEVER HAS TO BE NAMED — read this before adding any capability here ═══
(2026-09-01, after making exactly this mistake in T496.)

`key` is OPTIONAL and always has been. A widget that declares none still HAS an identity: it is
DERIVED from its content — its name within the nearest keyed ancestor, then a per-scope index among
identically-named siblings — never from its position in the tree, because a positional one moves
whenever anything else changes. `nav::identity_of` is that answer; `docs/widgets.md` § "Everything
else gets an identity anyway" is the rule, written long before this phase.

So a capability keyed to identity must NEVER be gated on `Base::key` being present. I wrote
`.draggable()` to read `key` directly, which silently did nothing on every widget that had no reason
to be named, and forced an author to learn an internal rule before they could drag anything.
Antonio: *"this makes developers know about an internal API not common"* and *"we decided earlier
that key is optional. Each widget/component should autogenerate this value if possible."*

THE RULE FOR ANY NEW CAPABILITY THAT NEEDS TO KNOW *WHICH* WIDGET: take the declared `key` when
there is one, fall back to the derived identity when there is not. In this phase's code that is
`drag::resolve::drag_identity`, and it is deliberately ONE function read by both the gesture and the
resolution so they cannot disagree. Guard: `an_unnamed_widget_is_still_draggable`.

Why the declared key is used unscoped while the derived one is scoped: a right-click and a drag must
point at the same thing, and `nav::key_at` answers a right-click with the row's OWN name. The
derived identity is scoped by keyed ancestors (`col:1/pane:2`) because that is what keeps a
remembered hint letter on the right row when two docks show the same rows.

═══ WHY THIS IS FIRST, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NOTIFICATION PHASE ═══
Moved from F009 to F003 on 2026-08-28 — it was never notification-specific; notifications are only where it surfaced. It sits at the top of F003 because it is the foundation Antonio's FIRST RULE rests on: a component cannot own its own input until one dispatch walks the tree.

TWO SILENT FAILURES IN TWO DAYS, one new surface, two different subsystems:
1. The toast stack receives zero pointer events, so its × and action buttons never fire and hover falls through to the pane beneath.
2. `prefix+/` lettered ONLY the toast — the hint walk read every visible layer's root box as an occluder, and a ToastStack is Pct(1.0) square because it POSITIONS its cards, not because it covers the screen. Fixed 2026-08-28 by reading the layer's own `covers_content` declaration, which the action router already honoured and the hint walk did not.

That is the shape of the defect: rebuild, layout, paint, hints and input are five separate walks over the layer stack, each with its own idea of what a layer means, and nothing checking they agree. Every new surface — a plugin's overlay included — must get it right in each one, and gets no error when it does not.

⚠️ AND THE SAME SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN (T495, 2026-09-01): a surface's BOX was taken for its input area. A box is routinely bigger than what a surface draws — a notification stack spans the window so a corner means the SCREEN's corner — so an empty invisible surface swallowed every press in the app and the chrome beneath stopped answering the mouse, with nothing failing anywhere. Now a seated surface passes the pointer through where it covers nothing (the browser's `pointer-events: none` on a positioned wrapper); its children still take what lands on them, and one that means to swallow says so through `overlay_occludes`, which `Overlay::blocking(true)` answers for the whole viewport. The seat sets that, so no author writes it and none can get it wrong.

═══ THE AUTHORITY ═══
`docs/surface-compositor.md` § 0 — the whole picture, and what AGENTS.md already flags as required reading before adding any layer or surface. Read it before planning any task here.

DONE 2026-08-28: `docs/input-architecture.md` was folded into it whole (now a redirect stub) so there is one voice rather than two, and AGENTS.md § 0d carries the FIRST RULE.

⚠️ CORRECTION: an earlier version of this description said `docs/hint-architecture.md` asserts "No second dispatch path" and that this is false. It is NOT false. Read in context, that sentence is about a **pick** propagating through the existing walk rather than introducing its own — which is correct. It is *pointer* input that has sixteen paths, not the picker.

═══ SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT HERE ═══
Priority order: T494+T495 (layer roots as tree children, modal as a swallowing node) landed first — both DONE and driven. Then T496 (chrome's 8 functions), T497 (pane header), T499 (HintSurface collapses to a tree path — 25 match sites across four files).

**T498 is CANCELED.** "Terminal viewport becomes a leaf node" duplicated P094(F011)/T449 from the input end. P097 owns the dispatch; P094 owns the terminal, and P094 depends on this phase.

T501/T502 are the plugin-capability half: a described plugin overlay gets input for free once this lands, but it still cannot BUILD what the exposé builds. Until one of our own overlays is built the way a plugin must build it (T502), "plugins can add overlays" is a claim, not a fact.

⚠️ MUST NOT be interleaved with the oversized-file splits — T466/T468/T470/T471/T472 carve up the same files (component.rs's router, event.rs, app/interaction.rs) and are deferred until this lands.

VERIFICATION: input routing is exactly where green tests prove nothing — the toast received no events for an unknown time and nothing errored. Antonio drives every surface's mouse behaviour (T500).

decisions: A surface is PLACED, never registered: chrome::place_surface puts it in the window root, keyed, replacing in place under the same key; chrome::remove_surface takes it out.

The window root lives on AppState, is NOT an Option, and the chrome is its child 0 rather than the root itself — the chrome is rebuilt on resize/sidebar-toggle/theme-reload and dropped outright by reload_config, so a surface parented to it would lose its open state, its half-played arrival and its focus.
seat_chrome finds the chrome slot BY KEY, not by position: a surface may be placed before the first chrome exists (the toast mounts at startup) and a positional child 0 would seat the chrome over it.

InteractionSource::Surface carries a SurfaceKey derived from the key a surface declares, not a LayerId — a registry id stops existing once a surface is a node, and a plugin can declare a key but can never obtain a LayerId. Derived from what the caller holds rather than looked up, because a surface builds its emitter BEFORE registering.

The registry keeps ONLY name, nesting, modality, covers_content, visibility and the ViewNode a described surface was described by. The live tree is a child of the window root, found by chrome::surface_node(_mut).
THE TREE TICKS; THE REGISTRY ONLY RECONCILES — leaving_before_tick() before window_root.tick(dt), retire_finished_exits() after. The registry must never advance a surface again.
The frost is Overlay::frosted(true), recorded into the scene's BASE band (never the deferred overlay band) and performed by the host between the base flush and the overlay band.

- `971b1e2` — **the remaining three surfaces** (exposé, command palette, `OverlayHost` modals + context menus). Gate green throughout (667 heca tests; clippy at the two known pre-existing warnings).

═══ ⚠️ OPEN REGRESSION — Antonio, driving, 2026-08-31 ═══

Introduced by `971b1e2`. **The exposé's animation:**
1. Zoom-OUT stalls at roughly 10–15% opacity.
2. **Moving the mouse completes it** — so nothing is requesting the next frame, and any input event kicks it. That is a frame-scheduling symptom, not an animation-maths one.
3. After the first open, subsequent zoom-INs show the same stall.
4. After that, `ctrl+h/j/k/l` are broken too.

PRIME SUSPECT, unverified — instrument before changing code:
- **A hidden surface is still a child of the window root.** `layout_layers`/`paint_layers` used to filter on `visible`, so a hidden layer was inert. Now its node stays in the tree: it is still ticked, still walked, and can still hold `Base::focused` — which would explain (4), the keys going to a surface that is not on screen.
- **Double tick.** `heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs:111` `state.window_root.tick(dt)` now ticks every surface as a child, and `:127` `state.layers.tick(&mut state.window_root, dt)` ticks them again. Both are consequences of the same thing: the registry's tick was written when it owned the trees and nothing else walked them.

tasks.title: Modal becomes a node that swallows what it does not handle
tasks.description:
GOAL: delete dispatch_modal_pointer and the keyboard special-casing for top_modal in heca/src/app/events.rs. A modal is just a node in the one tree that returns Handled::Yes for every event it does not otherwise consume, so nothing leaks to the page behind it.

PRESERVE: Esc / scrim-click dismiss, Tab/Shift+Tab focus cycling inside a Dialog, Ctrl+h/j/k/l inside a Dialog, the universal prefix+/ hint picker reaching a modal's buttons, and that a right-press that just opened the context menu is not also forwarded to the terminal.

VERIFY: Antonio drives — open the confirm dialog, click a button, Esc, scrim-click, Tab between buttons, prefix+/ onto a dialog button, and confirm the terminal never sees a stray click while a modal is up.

═══ SESSION STATE 2026-09-01 — BOTH HALVES BUILT + DRIVEN; two defects found and fixed; uncommitted ═══

POINTER HALF. dispatch_modal_pointer is gone. The host no longer asks the registry which modal is in front and dispatches into that node; it asks the TREE whether a surface owns the point under the pointer (overlay_occluded_at on window_root) and hands the event to the one walk, which picks the front-most itself. New funnel: chrome::dispatch_surface_pointer. CursorMoved / MouseInput / MouseWheel go through it; CursorLeft lost a duplicate — the cancel was delivered to the modal AND again to the whole tree. pointer_funnel.rs lint renamed to the new funnel.

TWO SHAPES REJECTED — do not retry either:
1. Gating on "is any surface grabbing input" (an overlay_active tree scan). The page feeds the same tree again further down, so a surface that DECLINES an event (a toast when the click misses a card) receives the raw press twice — and the framework pairs a click out of the halves, so you get two clicks. The gate must be positional and decisive: ask BEFORE the event moves; deliver here and stop, or touch nothing.
2. Targeting through FocusManager::offer_to_overlay. It picks the first focusable, not the front-most — the 2026-08-11 bug where a click on a confirm dialog's Close reached the map behind.

DECIDED BY ANTONIO 2026-09-01 — a context menu no longer swallows clicks page-wide. The app registers a menu as a modal layer, but the ContextMenu widget deliberately declares it does not occlude (so a second right-click can re-anchor). Sourcing the answer from the tree makes the widget win: with a menu open, a click on a pane now dismisses the menu AND focuses that pane, where before it only dismissed. He was shown the trade and said "current behavior is ok for me". Do NOT fix this back.

KEYBOARD HALF. events.rs no longer names a modal node for a key. The three sites that did — key press, key release, ModifiersChanged — hand the event to the window root and let delivery follow focus. The gate is layer_holds_keyboard, which asks app::input::focused_surface (the same rule AGENTS.md § Keybinding Style states) whether a LAYER is in front. A dock is deliberately excluded: a focused container answers keys through the actions it declared (T352-T355), and offering it the raw key here as well would be a second door onto one input. ModifiersChanged lost its gate entirely — it is an announcement and the framework broadcasts it; delivering only to the front-most modal meant every other surface tracked modifiers only while it happened to be in front. top_modal_node_mut is deleted. top_modal survives in events.rs at ONE place only, the opened_context_menu guard, which is about coverage, not routing.

NEW TEST: a_key_dispatched_at_the_window_root_reaches_a_placed_surface (chrome/layers/tests.rs). Nothing exercised the focus half of a seating before, because the old path reached a modal whether or not it held focus — so the failure it guards is a dialog that answers no key at all with every test green. It places a real Dialog and asserts Tab arrives through the root. A Handled::No there means fix the FOCUS, never add a routing predicate. ⚠️ A first version of this test failed and the CODE was right: it put the handler on a non-focusable child, and keys do not descend into the target's children (AGENTS § 0c). Assert on a widget that holds focus itself.

tasks.title: Chrome's 8 dispatch functions collapse into the walk
tasks.description:
GOAL: delete the 8 chrome_dispatch_* wrappers and route chrome pointer/widget input through the single tree walk.

⚠️ THE ORIGINAL "CURRENT STATE" IN THIS TASK WAS STALE. Those 8 functions no longer reach into `state.chrome_tree` — T494 moved every one of them to `state.window_root`, so "route chrome input through the one walk" was already true when this task was picked up. What is actually left is (a) eight thin wrappers around one call, and (b) the real blocker: the event loop cannot send ONE event per device event, because the app asks its own drag question before the tree may claim a press (F003/P085/T368). Antonio chose the full version: make the row own its dragging so that ordering stops existing.

═══ DONE SO FAR (2026-09-01, uncommitted, gates green, DnD driven and confirmed by Antonio) ═══

1. A DRAG IDENTITY IS THE NAME THE ROW ALREADY DECLARES. `.draggable()` / `.drop_target()` take no
argument; what is dragged is the widget's own identity. DELETED from the widget layer: the opaque
`DragItemId` a host registry handed out, and — the reason a plugin could never drag at all — the
closed `DragSurfaceId` enum listing which surfaces were allowed to (one entry: LeftSidebar).
`drag::resolve::drag_identity` is the ONE answer both the gesture and the resolution read: the
declared key when there is one (unscoped, so a right-click and a drag point at the same thing —
`nav::key_at`), the derived identity when there is not (`nav::identity_of`). ⚠️ See the phase
description: NEVER gate a capability on `Base::key` being present. Guard:
`an_unnamed_widget_is_still_draggable`.

2. THE WIDGETS DRAW THEIR OWN DRAG FEEDBACK. `component::paint_drag_feedback`, called from
`paint_child` beside the hint letter — one place every widget already passes through, so nothing
opts in. The target under the cursor draws the insertion line (or the swap outline when Shift is
held); the source draws a picture of itself under the pointer, in the overlay band so nothing
clips it. `PointerState` gained `drag_side`, `drag_pos` and `drag_mods` so a widget can answer
without measuring. This is the shape every other DnD library settled on (Flutter's DragTarget
rebuilds with what is over it; SwiftUI/HTML show a picture of the dragged view by default; the
follower lives in a top layer).

3. The app's map is keyed by name now (`DragItemRegistry`: name → pane/column/workspace). A name is
never parsed by the host — the component that wrote it is the only thing that says what it means,
exactly as `Provider::context_path` answers for menus.

═══ WHAT REMAINS — ONE INDIVISIBLE CHANGE, NOT YET STARTED ═══

The app still intercepts the press, so its OLD machine is what actually runs a drag today and the
new feedback never appears. Removing it is one piece:
- `mouse.rs`: delete the `drag_source` early-return block AND the `point_in_right_sidebar` /
  `point_in_top_bar` early returns that consume a press before the drag question.
- Deliver the drop as an EVENT instead of reading it out of app state at release: the rows'
  `on_drop` records source key + target key + side + swap into a small queue on `AppState`, drained
  in `render_frame` beside `drain_pending_menus` — the same sink pattern declared menus already use,
  which is how a widget hands the host something needing `&mut AppState`. The DECISION code in
  `mouse/release.rs` (move/swap a pane, move a column, drop a column on a workspace, and a column
  drag ignoring the pane cards nested in it) stays exactly as it is; only its trigger changes.
- Then delete: `mouse/drag.rs`, the `DragContext`/`DragPhase`/`SurfaceDragState` usage, the
  `ghost_label` plumbing, and the app's own drag painting in `chrome/scene.rs` (~1,500 lines touched
  across six files, mixed in with window resizing and floating-pane interactive move, which are
  DIFFERENT things and must not be swept up).

⚠️ ANTONIO FOUND THE PROOF THIS IS THE RIGHT FIX, 2026-09-01: panes drag in the LEFT sidebar and
not in the RIGHT one, though it is the same component. Two hardcoded reasons, both in the app's
machine: a press anywhere in the right sidebar is consumed before the drag question is asked
("the right sidebar has no drag surface yet"), and the machine is keyed by that closed one-entry
surface list. Nothing about the component differs. When the machine goes, both sidebars — and a
plugin's panel, and an overlay — drag for the same reason: the row says it can.

PRESERVE: sidebar hover cues on move; a press taken by the scrollbar thumb not also reading as a
press on the card behind it; a release reaching the tree wherever the cursor drifted; wheel over a
hovered sidebar scroll region not also scrolling the terminal; and a press that never becomes a drag
still focusing the pane (this comes free — a row turns a press and release into a click).

VERIFY: Antonio drives BOTH sidebars — hover cues, click a row, scroll, drag a pane, drag a column,
drop a column on a workspace, drag the scrollbar thumb and release off it.

tasks.title: Declarative arms for the widgets a plugin overlay needs
tasks.description:
GOAL: close the described-widget coverage gap so a plugin can actually build an overlay, not just be promised one. This is the CAPABILITY half of plugin overlays — the plumbing half falls out of the one-tree work; this does not.

CURRENT STATE (verified in code):
- 13 of 46 grid-ui widgets have NO declarative (ViewNode) form: CardGrid, ChromeRegion, CommandPalette, ContextMenu, Dialog, FocusScope, KeyHint, NfIcon, Pane, Progress, Spinner, Tooltip, Visibility. (Name-based check across heca-view / heca-view-realize; CardGrid verified directly twice.)
- Some are host-only BY DESIGN and stay that way: ChromeRegion, Pane, FocusScope.
- CardGrid — the widget the exposé cursor is built on — has zero references in heca-view or heca-view-realize. A described tree cannot construct one today.
- The declarative path: heca/src/chrome/view.rs (ViewNode / WidgetKind), heca/src/chrome/realize.rs (the recursive host mapper), plus the widget's own arm. Precedent: Dialog::body_boxed for a realized subtree; Choice children for options.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (Antonio) — A MENU IS A DECLARATION, NOT A WIDGET KIND.
An earlier version of this task reasoned that "Dialog/ContextMenu/CommandPalette are composed widgets a plugin would more likely build from parts" and leaned toward leaving the menu out of the described set. That is the wrong shape and must not be restored.

A context menu is not something an author assembles and places — it is a declaration attached to a row, the same way a press or a hint is. The native path already proves it: `.context_menu(menu)` is one builder on ANY widget (heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs), universal like `key`, with no row identity, no path string, no registered builder, no host hit test and no anchor — the framework takes the anchor from whatever triggered it.

So the described form is the SAME declaration on any node — a menu on the node, exactly as `on_hint` is on every node — never a `ContextMenu` kind a plugin must construct, size and position. Two authoring paths over one input that do not converge are the drift this project forbids (⭐⭐ RULE ZERO, "one door, never two"); a plugin that has to build a menu out of parts is writing the second path by hand and will get the anchor, the dismissal and the keyboard half only approximately right.

Today the split is: a RUST provider contributes menu entries by name (`Provider::context_path` names the row kind, `Provider::context_menus` returns entries carrying an Intent), while a plugin that builds its UI as a DESCRIBED tree cannot attach a menu to its own row at all. That is the concrete second-class path this task closes.

WORK:
- Decide, per non-host-only widget, whether a plugin overlay realistically needs it. CardGrid, Tooltip, Visibility, Spinner, Progress, KeyHint are the likely yes set.
- The MENU is not on that list because it is not a kind: give `ViewNode` the menu **declaration** (a menu on any node, its entries carrying Intents) so a described row gets the identical picker, anchor, dismissal and keyboard handling the native one gets, with nothing written. Check `Dialog` and `CommandPalette` for the same question before adding a kind for either — a modal body is already described data (ModalSpec), so what a plugin lacks may also be a declaration rather than a widget.
- For each in the yes set: add a WidgetKind (or slot/prop on an existing kind), a realize.rs arm, props resolved against Theme, events wired to Intent, the showcase demo, and docs/widgets.md — per the "creating new widgets / documentation is mandatory" rule in AGENTS.md.
- CardGrid is the important one: it carries a navigable cursor, so its described form must hand back navigable cells (Vec<GridCell>) the way a component does, not reach into a registry (RULE ZERO).
- The every_widget_kind_realizes_to_a_live_widget_except_the_host_only_ones test must stay green and its host-only allowlist updated deliberately.

DOES NOT need the one-tree work to start, but is only useful once it lands. ~1-2 days. A new WidgetKind is host-side (view.rs + realize.rs) but the widget arm may touch heca-grid-ui.
